our data show the average fission neutron energies to be in agreement with previously published data.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the average fission neutron energies do not increase significantly with the inducing neutron energy for up to 5 MeV, but above 5 Me V the average fission energy increases significantly.
the average fission neutron energies are not significantly higher than those of Watt-spectrum fits, which are used in most nuclear reactor calculations.
the fission spectra of 235U can be accurately described by the Watt spectrum for energies up to 10MeV, and that there is no indication of second-chance fissions in the energy range studied.
